vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agent-chronicle
Version: 0.6.2

The skill is designed for AI diary generation, operating primarily through local file system interactions and OpenClaw's `sessions_spawn` mechanism for LLM interaction. It explicitly removed direct HTTP calls in v0.6.0, enhancing security. File operations are confined to the workspace's `memory/diary/` directory. While `pandoc` and `weasyprint` are used for export, `pandoc` includes a `--sandbox` flag, and `weasyprint` processes internally generated HTML with a local base URL, mitigating potential execution risks. The skill constructs prompts for a sub-agent using local session data, which could be a prompt injection vector if a user intentionally inputs malicious instructions into their own session logs, but the skill itself does not exhibit malicious intent and instructs the main agent to limit the sub-agent's output to markdown. No evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized remote control, persistence mechanisms, or obfuscation was found.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and requirements are consistent with a diary/journal generator for agents; it reads local agent 'memory' files and writes diary files but does not request unrelated credentials or outbound endpoints beyond an optional CSS fetch for HTML exports.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (agent diary) aligns with what the skill does: it gathers session logs and persistent diary files, builds a generation task for a sub-agent (sessions_spawn), and saves/export diary files. Required binary (python3) and optional dependencies (pandoc/weasyprint) match the read/write/export functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts read session logs (memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md) and persistent diary files (memory/diary/*.md) to build context — this is expected for a diary. The SKILL.md instructs agents to spawn sub-agents via OpenClaw's sessions_spawn rather than making raw HTTP calls. Be aware the skill will read potentially sensitive conversation/session logs (local workspace memory) to create entries and, if configured, append summaries back into daily memory files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only) so nothing is automatically downloaded. There are local Python scripts; exporting to PDF/HTML requires external tools: pandoc (export.py) or Python packages/weasyprint + markdown (export_pdf.py). These are normal for export features but you should install/inspect those dependencies before running exports.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no credentials and no special environment variables. It does consult OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE or AGENT_WORKSPACE (if set) to locate the workspace memory; this is proportional for a skill that reads/writes agent memory files.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not force-included (always:false) and does not request elevated platform privileges. It writes files under the agent workspace (config.json and memory/diary/*) which is expected for a diary tool. Auto-generation is configurable (default disabled in example), so it will not run automatically unless explicitly enabled.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says: a diary generator that reads your agent's local session logs and persistent diary files and writes diary entries back into the workspace. Before installing or running it, consider: 1) The script reads memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md and memory/diary/* — those files can contain sensitive user or conversation data, so ensure the workspace path it finds (OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE, AGENT_WORKSPACE, or default locations) is the intended location. 2) Setup may create config.json and diary files; review config.example.json to confirm privacy/auto_generate settings. 3) Exports: export.py requires pandoc (and may fetch a CSS file from a CDN for HTML exports); export_pdf.py requires Python packages (weasyprint, markdown). If you have network restrictions or sensitive environments, be aware of the optional external CSS fetch. 4) Because generation is intended to run as a spawned sub-agent (sessions_spawn), confirm your platform's sub-agent permissions and where sub-agent outputs will be sent. If you want extra caution, inspect/grep the scripts locally and run them in a restricted/sandboxed workspace before giving the skill access to a production workspace.
